title: Levioso: Efficient Compiler-Informed Secure Speculation
problem: Spectre-type attacks exploit speculative execution to leak secrets through multiple transmission channels. Existing hardware-only defenses lack program knowledge and conservatively restrict all potentially-leaking instructions, incurring substantial performance overhead.
motivation: Modern CPU performance depends on speculative execution, but this feature enables exploitable side-channel vulnerabilities that leak sensitive information.
method: Levioso combines the compiler (the program that turns code into CPU instructions) with the CPU hardware itself to stop Spectre attacks more efficiently. The compiler reads through code and identifies which instructions could leak secrets through side channels—invisible escape routes where data seeps out via timing clues or CPU cache behavior—then gives this list to the hardware. The hardware uses this list to selectively block speculative execution (the CPU's practice of guessing which code path to take and running ahead) only at those risky points, instead of blocking all guessing. This prevents both leaks that happen during speculation and leaks that occur even when the CPU isn't speculating.
key_novelty: The core idea is using the compiler to identify exactly which instructions leak secrets, so hardware can selectively block speculative execution only at those points rather than applying conservative blanket restrictions that harm performance.
contributions: Compiler analysis to identify instruction-level leak points
Selective speculation restrictions guided by program knowledge
Efficient defense against both speculative and non-speculative information leaks
